tldr: Stakeholders identify insufficient development-ready sites as a competitive constraint, citing lack of infrastructure funding, high costs of facility expansion (water, sewer, utility, transportation upgrades), and a disconnect between policy land definitions and market reality in Urban Growth Boundary inventories. They call for expanded, accelerated, and better-coordinated funding and tools.

bullets.text: Lack of development-ready sites identified as key constraint limiting competitiveness
Oregon lacks sufficient supply of sites with characteristics needed for traded-sector opportunities
Many communities lack infrastructure funding required to prepare sites for development
Businesses cite extraordinary costs of facility expansion (water, sewer, utility, transportation upgrades) that delay investment decisions
UGB land definitions: "available" and "suitable" diverge from market reality
Inventories are technically compliant but functionally unusable for near-term investment
Disconnect between policy definitions and market reality creates uncertainty for businesses and limits practical land supply
Stakeholders report existing policies, programs, and tools need expansion, acceleration, better coordination, and increased funding
